g.text: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on long chain-of-thought (CoT) demonstrations
has emerged as a critical technique for developing reasoning-capable
language models (Wei et al., 2022; DeepSeek-AI et al., 2025).
g.title: N1 [Context] (cites=2) Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on long chain-of-thought (CoT) demonstrations has emerged as a critical technique for developing reasoning-capable language models (Wei et al., 2022; DeepSeek-AI et al., 2025).

In this paradigm, models learn to produce extended reasoning traces before

g.title: N2 [Context] (cites=0) In this paradigm, models learn to produce extended reasoning traces before arriving at final answers, enabling improved performance on complex mathematical and scientific problems.

g.text: Kopiczko: many epochs on small data wins
However, recent work by Kopiczko et al. (2026) reveals a counterintuitive
phenomenon: under a fixed gradient-update budget, training for many epochs
on a small dataset substantially outperforms single-epoch training on a
g.title: N3 [Prior_Work] (cites=1) However, recent work by Kopiczko et al. (2026) reveals a counterintuitive phenomenon: under a fixed gradient-update budget, training for many epochs on a small dataset substantially outperforms single-epoch training on a larger dataset.

g.title: N4 [Prior_Work] (cites=0) On AIME and GPQA benchmarks, models trained for 32 epochs on 1,600 samples achieve approximately double the accuracy of models trained for 1 epoch on 51,200 samples.

g.text: This "repetition advantage" challenges conventional machine learning

g.title: N5 [Limitation] (cites=0) This "repetition advantage" challenges conventional machine learning intuition, where more unique training samples typically yield better generalization.

g.text: Why does repetition help so dramatically?
Why does data repetition help so dramatically in long-CoT SFT?
g.title: N6 [Limitation] (cites=0) Why does data repetition help so dramatically in long-CoT SFT?

g.text: One possibility is that repeated exposure to the same examples
enables deeper learning of reasoning patterns.
g.title: N6a [Limitation: hypothesis-A] (cites=0) One possibility is that repeated exposure to the same examples enables deeper learning of reasoning patterns.

g.text: An alternative hypothesis is that the advantage stems not from
improved reasoning, but from better learning of output format and
termination behavior—the ability to reliably produce parseable
final answers rather than truncated or…
g.title: N6b [Limitation: hypothesis-B] (cites=0) An alternative hypothesis is that the advantage stems not from improved reasoning, but from better learning of output format and termination behavior—the ability to reliably produce parseable final answers rather than truncated or malformed outputs.

g.text: We investigate this question through a diagnostic framework that
decomposes accuracy into two components: ParseRate (the fraction
of generations with extractable final answers) and Acc|Parse
g.title: N7 [Method] (cites=0) We investigate this question through a diagnostic framework that decomposes accuracy into two components: ParseRate (the fraction of generations with extractable final answers) and Acc|Parse (accuracy conditioned on successful parsing).

g.text: This decomposition reveals whether accuracy differences arise from
g.title: N8 [Method] (cites=0) This decomposition reveals whether accuracy differences arise from termination behavior or reasoning quality.

g.text: Our mediation analysis shows that the repetition advantage is
almost entirely a termination effect: on AIME benchmarks, the
accuracy gap between repetition and scaling conditions reverses
when conditioning on successful parsing, with…
g.title: N9 [Result] (cites=0) Our mediation analysis shows that the repetition advantage is almost entirely a termination effect: on AIME benchmarks, the accuracy gap between repetition and scaling conditions reverses when conditioning on successful parsing, with mediation fractions exceeding 1.0.

g.text: Data scaling wins when both terminate
The data-scaling condition actually produces better reasoning when both
g.title: N10 [Result] (cites=0) The data-scaling condition actually produces better reasoning when both models terminate properly.

g.text: Based on this insight, we propose Termination-Aware SFT, a simple
modification that increases the loss weight on termination tokens
g.title: N11 [Method] (cites=0) Based on this insight, we propose Termination-Aware SFT, a simple modification that increases the loss weight on termination tokens (</think> and EOS).

g.text: This intervention improves ParseRate and accuracy over standard
SFT, though it recovers only 14% of the repetition advantage,
suggesting that termination learning through repetition involves
mechanisms beyond what explicit loss reweighting…
g.title: N12 [Result] (cites=0) This intervention improves ParseRate and accuracy over standard SFT, though it recovers only 14% of the repetition advantage, suggesting that termination learning through repetition involves mechanisms beyond what explicit loss reweighting can capture.
